description.narrative:
For over seven years, women shellfish collectors in Tunisian coastal areas such as Sfax, Gabès, Zarzis, and Djerba have suffered from forced unemployment due to declining marine stocks and the worsening effects of climate change on ecosystems and coastalproduction.
These women are among the most economically and socially vulnerable groups, relying for years on shellfish collection as their main source of income to support their families. However, climate change, rising water temperatures, salinity changes, and coastal pollution have significantly reduced production, leading many women to lose their livelihoods. They often work in difficult, informal conditions without social protection or official recognition as maritime workers. They also face increasing challenges related to food security, public health, and degradation of coastal ecosystems.
Despite this, these women demonstrate resilience by seeking sustainable alternatives such as exploiting invasive species like the blue crab or contributingto habitat restoration and environmental awareness initiatives. The appearance of the blue crab, driven by temperature and salinity changes, offers an alternative opportunity to adapt and create new income sources.
In this context, the project aims toestablish a “Blue Justice Lab” as a participatory space bringing together women shellfish collectors in Sfax, young researchers, and local stakeholders to co-create innovative solutionsfor climate adaptation and improved livelihoods. The project focusesonempowering women with new skills to valorize the blue crab and transform it into sustainable craft, agricultural, and food products, while encouraging young researchers to develop practical innovations.
The lab will also contribute to a national climate justice vision from a gender perspective through an advocacy brief highlighting the realities of coastal women and their right to decent work and dignified living.
Project outcomes The project aims to establish a Blue Justice Lab to empower women shellfish collectors in facing climate change by creating an innovative community space that brings together women, young researchers, and local stakeholders to co-develop solutions for climate adaptation and sustainable livelihoods.
It begins with anational hackathon and ideathon based on design thinking, involving 10 young researchers, experts, and 30 women shellfish collectors to generate innovative ideas addressing environmental and economic challenges. This hackathon serves as a starting pointfor developing practical prototypes in the blue economy, invasive species utilization, and social/environmental innovation.
The blue crab is a central model: the project aims to transform it from an environmental threat into a local economicresource throughsustainable value chains. Women will gain practical training to turn it into value-added craft, agricultural, and food products, enhancing economic independence and resilience.
Young researchers will analyze the scientific and economic aspects ofinvasive species and develop practical solutions, bridging academic knowledge and local needs.
An advocacy note between Tunisia andMorocco will highlight the challenges faced by coastal women and advocate for their rights to climate justice and decent work. Expected results: • Train 30 women in sustainable valorization of shellfish and blue crab • Train 10 young researchers in blue innovation • Implement at least 2 local climate adaptation pilot projects • Produce a national and regional advocacy briefon climate justice

participating-org.narrative:
The Tunisian Maritime Cluster is an association founded in 2019, bringing together stakeholders from the private sector, academia, and civil society committed to the sustainable and innovative development of the blue economy in Tunisia. Public institutions participate as external partners.
Since its creation, the Cluster has established itself as a strategic platform for collaboration, fostering synergies between the various stakeholders in the maritime sector. Its areas of action cover a wide range of activities, from fishing and shipbuilding to maritime transport, coastal tourism, and the preservation of the marine environment.
